Consistent with Ferguson's stated 'enforcement over rulemaking' posture. But this does not mean lighter-touch treatment in practice: enforcement under the existing, unrevised guides has tightened through 2024-2025, with carbon-neutral, biodegradable, and unqualified-recyclability claims all triggering real consent decrees. Net effect: the text isn't moving, but enforcement risk under it is not relaxing either — the same 'stable but with a real countervailing dynamic' pattern as UK_pEPR below

evidence: The European Commission announced its intent to withdraw the Green Claims Directive proposal on 20 Jun 2025 — two days after an EPP letter (18 Jun 2025) explicitly called for withdrawal, citing requirements that were 'overly complex, administratively burdensome, and costly.' The same EPP-led simplification pattern that also produced the Omnibus I (CSRD/CSDDD) outcome and the second EUDR delay, now landing on a fourth file. Status remains technically unresolved — the Commission has not formally terminated the proposal, and Parliament committee chairs have signaled readiness to resume negotiations, so a revival isn't ruled out. The separate, already-adopted EmpCo directive is unaffected and proceeds on its own track (see the EmpCo row below)

key_actors: European Commission (infringement enforcement); 20 lagging member states including Belgium, Spain, France, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Portugal
evidence: EmpCo (Directive (EU) 2024/825) is a separate, already-adopted directive from the withdrawn Green Claims Directive proposal above — it is not being weakened. Member states had until 27 Mar 2026 to transpose it into national law; on 28 May 2026 the Commission opened infringement procedures (letters of formal notice) against 20 member states for failing to do so. The rules become binding EU-wide from 27 Sep 2026 regardless of transposition status in the laggard states. Germany and Italy, among others, had fully transposed it as of June 2026. This is a member-state administrative-compliance-lag story, not a left/right ideological vote — marked 'mixed' rather than forced onto a left/right axis

key_actors: European Parliament (426 in favour, 125 against, 74 abstentions, adopted Nov 2024); Council final adoption Dec 2024
evidence: PPWR passed with a broad cross-party majority (426-125-74) — well before the 2025-2026 EPP-led simplification wave that later hit CSRD/CSDDD/EUDR/Green Claims. Widely reported as 'the most lobbied political process in the EU's history' during drafting, but the final vote margin shows it wasn't a narrow ideological win the way the later Omnibus-era votes were. Worth re-checking once it's actually in force and post-application lobbying resumes, but no active simplification push was found this pass
